step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates an automated road defect inspection system using serverless and machine learning components on AWS. Engineers (UserCompanyAgent) upload video recordings via a web UI (UserCompanyWebsite). Raw video files are saved directly into an S3 bucket. The web UI triggers AWS Elemental MediaConvert to split high-definition video into thousands of individual frames. Once split, MediaConvert passes frames to parallel Lambda functions containing containerized TensorFlow machine learning models trained via Amazon SageMaker. The inference Lambdas perform defect detection on each frame and write metadata and defect records to DynamoDB. Engineer validation/rejection feedback in DynamoDB is picked up by a training pipeline Lambda to continually retrain the SageMaker model in a feedback loop.

graph.name: AWS Automated Road Defect Inspection Architecture
graph.notes: Serverless pipeline processes tens of thousands of video frames in parallel using Elemental MediaConvert, Lambda containers with SageMaker ML models, and DynamoDB.

nodes.name: ENGINEERS
nodes.notes: Road inspection engineers who upload video clips and review/validate detected defects.

nodes.name: UI
nodes.notes: Web application deployed on AWS for uploading inspection video and displaying results.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: S3 bucket storing raw inspection video files uploaded from UI.

nodes.name: ELEMENTAL MEDIACONVERT
nodes.notes: AWS Elemental MediaConvert used to split uploaded video files into individual frames.

nodes.name: SAGEMAKER
nodes.notes: Amazon SageMaker used to train ML model on annotated images with road defects.

nodes.name: LAMBDA (Inference)
nodes.notes: Containerized Lambda functions running in parallel to perform ML inference on video frames using TensorFlow model.

nodes.name: DYNAMODB
nodes.notes: DynamoDB table storing frame metadata, defect records, and deduplication logic data.

nodes.name: LAMBDA (Training Pipeline)
nodes.notes: Lambda function triggering automated retraining pipeline based on rejected/validated feedback from engineers in DynamoDB.

edges.notes: Engineers upload video recordings to the web UI.
Web UI stores raw video files in S3 bucket.
Web UI triggers Elemental MediaConvert job to split video into frames.
Elemental MediaConvert feeds video frames to inference Lambda functions.
SageMaker model is packaged and deployed into Lambda container image.
Inference Lambda functions store metadata and detected defects into DynamoDB.
DynamoDB provides defect feedback data to automated training pipeline Lambda.
Automated training pipeline Lambda updates metadata and state back to DynamoDB.
